title: He Has Not Thrown a Javelin in Competition Since September. India Has Named Neeraj Chopra for Glasgow Anyway.
excerpt: The AFI's 32-member squad for the Commonwealth Games includes Chopra on a conditional basis — he must prove his fitness in meets over the coming weeks before his place is confirmed.
body:
India's biggest athletics star is heading to the Commonwealth Games — probably.

The Athletics Federation of India on Sunday named a 32-member squad for the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, and Neeraj Chopra's name was on the list. But there was an asterisk beside it. The two-time Olympic medallist has been included on a conditional basis: he must prove his fitness in international meets over the coming weeks before his spot is confirmed.

It is a remarkable position for an athlete of Chopra's stature. He has not competed since the World Athletics Championships in Tokyo last September, where a back injury that he had concealed throughout the build-up limited him to an eighth-place finish — his worst result at a global championship since his breakthrough gold at the 2018 Commonwealth Games.

## The Long Road Back

AFI Selection Committee chairman Adille Sumariwalla, speaking at a virtual press conference on Sunday, explained the federation's reasoning. "Neeraj has recovered and he is ready to compete in the next few days," Sumariwalla said. "He asked us to add him and we expect him to play a few meets this month."

Chopra has spent the past seven months in rehabilitation — first in Türkiye, then at the Olympic Training Centre in Bienne, Switzerland, where he has been based since late May on a 47-day camp approved by the Mission Olympic Cell. His coach, Czech javelin legend Jan Zeležný, has been overseeing a phased return that prioritises longevity over rushed comebacks.

The conditional selection mirrors that of triple jumper Selva Prabhu, the NCAA champion from Kansas State who was born in Madurai. Both athletes were given the green light to earn their final confirmation through performances outside the domestic circuit.

## A Squad Built for Glasgow

The full 32-member squad features 22 men and 10 women. Among the confirmed names are 110m hurdles national record-holder Tejas Shirse, who clocked a stunning 13.27 seconds last week; long jumper M. Sreeshankar; and steeplechase specialist Parul Chaudhary, who broke the 5000m national record in Nice on Saturday.

In the javelin, Rohit Yadav and Yashvir Singh both cleared the CWG qualifying mark of 82.61m at the Indian Athletics Series on Saturday — a relief for selectors after World Championship finalist Sachin Yadav was ruled out with an elbow injury.

The Glasgow Games run from July 23 to August 2, followed by the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya from September 19 to October 4. For Chopra, the dense calendar means every competitive throw in the coming weeks will carry the weight of two major multi-sport events.

## What It Means for Diaspora Fans

For the estimated 1.6 million people of Indian origin in the United Kingdom, Chopra's potential presence at Hampden Park would be the marquee event of a summer packed with live Indian sport on British soil — coming in the same window as the Women's T20 World Cup in England.

Chopra won gold at his only previous Commonwealth Games appearance in Gold Coast 2018, throwing 86.47 metres as a 20-year-old. He skipped the 2022 edition in Birmingham. A return to the Games in Glasgow, where India has a passionate and vocal diaspora community, would carry enormous symbolic weight — if the javelin cooperates.

"Let's see how he performs," Sumariwalla said. For once, the whole country will be watching not for gold, but for proof that the body is ready.
